patch.objective: Sequence the conduction system (SA node, AV node, AV bundle, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers) and match the P wave, QRS complex and T wave to the events they record
secondaryObjectives: Interpret the oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve, including its shift to the right as temperature, carbon dioxide and acidity rise in working muscle

sources.cite: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Cardiac Muscle and Electrical Activity
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch: the SA node is the pacemaker; the impulse pauses about 100 ms at the AV node, passes the AV bundle and bundle branches to the Purkinje fibers; the P wave is atrial depolarization, the QRS complex ventricular depolarization, the T wave ventricular repolarization; an arrhythmia is 'a departure from the normal pattern of conduction and contraction', and in atrial fibrillation the ventricles may keep pumping. The case: during an ICU patient's first stand, the monitor shows a new irregular rhythm; stop and call the team.

sources.cite: APTA Acute Care and APTA Cardiovascular and Pulmonary, Adult Vital Sign Interpretation in Acute Care Guide 2021 (boards approved March and April 2021)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11 through a text extraction of the PDF. Normal exercise response: HR rises about 10 beats/min per MET and returns to the pre-exercise level in 3-5 min; SBP rises about 10 mmHg per MET. Stop criteria include SBP drop >10 mmHg with increasing workload, new or worsening dysrhythmia, RR >40, unable to speak comfortably, SpO2 <90% or a drop of 4% or more (acute coronary syndrome), SpO2 <85% (lung disease); lung disease activity target 88-92%. Orthostatic hypotension: SBP drop >20 or DBP drop >10 mmHg within 3 min of standing. Beta blockers: lower HR with exercise and a dampened BP response; use the RPE scale in addition to HR.

sources.cite: Hodgson CL, Stiller K, Needham DM, et al. Expert consensus and recommendations on safety criteria for active mobilization of mechanically ventilated critically ill adults. Crit Care. 2014;18:658. doi:10.1186/s13054-014-0658-y
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11 in a copy of the published PDF (the publisher's own PDF link could not be fetched). FiO2 below 0.6 with SpO2 above 90% and RR below 30/min were considered safe for in- and out-of-bed mobilization; vasoactive drugs are not in themselves a contraindication but rising doses call for caution; the most conservatively scored parameter takes precedence; oxygen reserve should exceed the activity. The traffic-light figures were not readable in the text, so no HR or MAP limit is taken from it. Written for ventilated patients; applied here to a patient on high-flow oxygen.
